newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ciba may be priced above Sfr 86/shr - UBS.
newsitem.headline: Ciba may be priced above Sfr 86/shr - UBS.

text.p: Shares of Ciba Specialty Chemicals Holding Inc may be priced above the indicated range of 72 to 86 Swiss francs per share for the global offering, co-lead arranger Union Bank of Switzerland said.

"In the light of the meaningful trading volumes seen in the Ciba Specialty Chemicals rights since the beginning of the rights trading period, the joint global coordinators have determined that the pricing for the global offering will be made principally by reference to the trading price in the rights at the time of pricing (as adjusted to take account of the 10 Swiss franc subscription price," UBS said in a statement.
CSFB is the other global coordinator for the issue.
"As a result, investors should be aware that the pricing may occur at levels above 86 Swiss francs per share, depending upon the trading price in the rights at the time."
A banking consortium last week set a minimum price of 64 Swiss francs it will pay for rights in Ciba, which is being spun off from Novartis via a one-for-one rights issue to Novartis shareholders.

The consortium will exercise the rights to get shares to be offered in a global offering with at least 300 million Swiss francs worth of stock. It was for this offer that the indicated range of 72 to 86 francs was set last month.
The rights, which began trading on February 26, have been holding well above this price amid strong demand. They were quoted around 96.75 francs today, valuing the shares at 106.75.
The consortium is scheduled to set its final rights bid price on Monday, March 10 at around 1800 GMT. Share trading starts on March 13.

A source familiar with the deal said the consortium still believed the indicative price range properly valued Ciba at up to 6.21 billion francs, but he added investors should be aware that the final price could be set above the indicated range.

"We just wanted to steer the market and make sure there was not any confusion about this slight change on the price range," he said. He added the group had not expected rights prices to remain as strong as they have amid strong retail demand.
Rights initially traded above 100 francs in the grey market.
"We still believe our valuation of the company to be correct and the company was happy with that at the outset, so we have just taken the 86 off the top," the source said.

"The price range is now between the 72 and the upper limit is effectively a moving limit, being the market price at the moment. This means at the moment it would be quite high and it may be above 86, so this is how we are playing it."
He said many retail investors were putting in orders "at best", but added institutions were taking a more price sensitive approach during book building.
